result.summary: Decouples Bitcoin Core's optional indexing architecture from internal node types like CBlockIndex and CChainState, shifting index synchronization out of src/index into a reusable node::SyncChain routine. It eliminates holding cs_main during index notification processing and aligns index event handling with interfaces::Chain for multiprocess support.
result.problem: Currently, indexing subsystems are tightly coupled to node validation internals and hold cs_main during parts of synchronization, causing lock contention and preventing indexes from running in separate processes. In addition, existing index startup and sync logic contains race conditions during reindexing.

open_concerns: The changeset is large and has historically suffered from commit churn, prompting discussion on whether to split parts (such as race fixes and initial refactors) into standalone PRs.
resolved_concerns: Fixed race conditions where indexes rewound blocks unnecessarily during -reindex-chainstate.
Resolved TSAN and ASAN issues regarding index synchronization threads and BlockFilterIndex filter mutex.
Cleaned up intermediate kernel boundary leaks by keeping BlockInfo in interfaces.

result.card: PR #24230 decouples the indexing system from internal node types (CBlockIndex, CChainState) and moves index synchronization logic into node::SyncChain, eliminating cs_main locking during notification handling. This addresses locking contention in index syncing and serves as essential leverage for running indexes out-of-process under the multiprocess project (#10102). The change enjoys strong concept and approach support from several contributors, though review progress has been slow due to the PR's size and merge conflicts that currently require a rebase.
